AgentCompass v0.7.8 removes steps the router used to hand back to the caller: a dispatch that is still being created, a schedule, a Workflow and a stale usage reading are now carried by the product.

- **A dispatch that is still being created finishes by itself.** When `roll` answers `pending`, its watcher finds the worker Paseo creates, binds it, settles the dispatch and notifies the parent. The caller is asked to run `next_argv` only where nothing would act after the command returns, and that command then carries the operation to its end.
- **A notification is promised only when something will send it.** Some hosts end every process a command starts when the command returns (Antigravity on Windows, measured). There the router promises a notification only while the tray is running, whose periodic pass restarts the watcher; without the tray the worker is told to report to its parent itself.
- **No second worker beside a resumed one.** A resume whose send timed out or lost its connection is no longer treated as refused: the worker stays bound and is observed. Relaunches, retries and replans are started only by an owner that may launch (the watcher, a `roll` of the same task, the tray's pass), and only inside the dispatch's life.
- **The gate routes a Paseo schedule itself.** Creating or changing a schedule no longer needs a plan made by hand first: the gate plans the schedule's prompt. On Antigravity and Pi the planned route is filled in; on Claude Code and Codex the call is refused once with the exact values to repeat.
- **A Workflow needs only the user's words**: `agentcompass record --trigger workflow --basis "<what the user asked>"`.
- **`plan` without `--hours`** asks the classifier for them; a cached usage reading of an earlier shape is collected again by the plan that needs it.
- **Tray: the pre-reset priority menu is your own list.** Choose in the settings page which models it offers (**Edit menu…**); each entry offers the expected time to the reset (1 to 24 hours; a nearer time is a stronger priority) in the tray menu and in the settings page, and its own cancel while in effect.

The full list is in the [changelog](https://github.com/akiiwa-games/AgentCompass-Router/blob/v0.7.8/CHANGELOG.md).

Verified on the released tree: the full test suite; the foreign-machine check F01 to F13; the zero-dispatch check over 13 surfaces, after two of its expectations were brought up to this version on the release runner (a worker told that no watcher reports for it reports itself, and the end notice follows); the published reference data against every released reader of its schema; the Windows Sandbox installer check. That a host ends a command's processes with the command was measured inside a real Antigravity command. An open-ended review of the whole version, in two parts, found seven defects that blocked the release (among them: a failed attempt nobody relaunched where the host ends the watcher with the command, a settled resume attached to the worker's next turn, a schedule route the gate named and then refused, a menu edit that dropped entries of the user's list); they and four smaller ones are fixed, each rule with a test seen failing first. Not exercised against live hosts in the review: the gate filling in a schedule call on Antigravity and Pi, which the hook's tests cover. The boards were not read again for this release. Left for a later version: a schedule created or changed through a wrapped call (`execute_code`, `mcp-cli`) and an `update_schedule` that changes only the prompt are not judged; a foreground `launch` that schedules a retry itself asks for `next_argv` once more instead of waiting the backoff out; 31 tray texts of earlier versions have no English entry.

The Windows tray installer is unsigned; Windows SmartScreen may warn on first launch. See [packaging/SIGNING.md](https://github.com/akiiwa-games/AgentCompass-Router/blob/v0.7.8/packaging/SIGNING.md).

Status: alpha. Accounts come from discovery on your machine; choose which ones take part in the tray.
